title: What does a lift lying on its side remind you of?
description: The endless lift is laid on its side so that up becomes right and down becomes left. Each floor of the lift lands on a number of the number line. Keeko's doubt is that a number line starts at zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: the infinite lift turned on its side is a number line, with positive numbers to the right and negative numbers to the left. Watch for students who think a number line must start at zero and stop there.

source: Take a look at the 'infinite lift' above. Does it remind you
video_script.why: The child sees that the endless lift, turned on its side, is the number line, with up matching right and down matching left.
video_script.substitution: The book's own infinite lift, laid on its side so that each level lands on a number.
video_script.anchor: the infinite lift of the book, with levels going up and down without end from level zero
video_script.wrong_answer: a number line starts at zero
video_script.wrong_move: believes a number line begins at zero, so a lift with levels below zero cannot match it
video_script.payoff_line: Turn the endless lift on its side and it is a number line.

final_answer.value: Yes: rotate the lift by 90 degrees and it is a number line
final_answer.spoken: yes, rotate the lift by ninety degrees and it is a number line

maths_rules: the lift turned by a quarter turn: up becomes right, down becomes left
level 0 stays at the middle; levels +1, +2, +3 go right, levels -1, -2, -3 go left
right is the forward (positive) direction, left is the backward (negative) direction
smaller numbers lie to the left of bigger numbers: -3 < 2, 2 < 5
slip: the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, ... alone go only to the right of 0; the line goes on to the left of 0 as well
video_script.design: The infinite lift is drawn upright, then turned on its side while its levels slide onto a line of numbers.
